facts.raw_span: crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years
denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
no prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported
occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting
C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal
HIV test was negative
substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate
thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum
sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas
AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive

concepts.why: The presence of noncaseating granulomas, destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses are consistent with Wegener's granulomatosis.
The presence of noncaseating granulomas, enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum, and destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with sarcoidosis.
The positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and the thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses are consistent with tuberculosis.
The presence of noncaseating granulomas and destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with chronic granulomatous sinusitis.
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and the destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with fungal sinusitis.
The presence of recurrent sinus infections and destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and the destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with allergic fungal sinusitis.
The presence of noncaseating granulomas and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum are consistent with granulomatous disease.
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and the destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with invasive aspergillosis.
The presence of recurrent sinus infections and destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates are consistent with chronic rhinosinusitis.

The combination of recurrent sinus infections, destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and noncaseating granulomas, along with a negative HIV test, points towards Granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

rationales.F05: Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates indicates severe sinus disease
rationales.F07: Negative HIV test reduces likelihood of certain infections
rationales.F11: Noncaseating granulomas are characteristic of granulomatous diseases
rationales.F12: Positive AFB PCR probe is diagnostic for tuberculosis
